plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional vector field plot drawn inside a light blue wireframe cube, with black x, y, and z axes running through it; x points toward the lower left, y to the right, and z vertically. A small shaded blue sphere sits where the axes cross, marked with the label 0, standing for a large mass at the origin. Arrows fill the interior of the cube and every one points inward toward that sphere. Those closest to the origin are long and bright orange, those at intermediate distance shorter and teal, and those near the corners and faces reduced to small dashes, so length and color together carry the magnitude of the field. Several of the longest arrows lie along the axis directions and meet the sphere head on. Because length and direction vary independently, the reader takes in both at once: the field aims at the central mass everywhere, and its strength climbs sharply as distance to the origin shrinks. The plot renders the gravitational field of a point mass, making visible the uniformly attractive radial direction and the rapid growth in magnitude near the source.

elements: light blue wireframe cube centered on the origin (edges ±2 world units)
vertical z-axis through the origin with arrowhead and label 'z' at top
y-axis through the origin pointing screen-right with arrowhead and label 'y'
x-axis through the origin pointing lower-left with arrowhead and label 'x'
small shaded blue sphere at the origin representing the central mass
origin label '0' sitting just below-right of the sphere
a grid of inward-pointing arrows filling the cube interior; every arrow aims at the origin
arrow color encodes magnitude: bright orange near the origin, teal at intermediate distance, tiny dark-teal dashes near corners/faces
highlighted sample point (larger marker) with its own oversized vector, controlled by the distance slider

interactions.teaches: Viewing the field from all sides shows every arrow aims at the central sphere — the field is radially inward everywhere in 3D, not just in the visible slice

interactions.label: Distance r from the central mass
interactions.teaches: Dragging the sample point inward makes its vector lengthen sharply (|g| ∝ 1/r²) and shift from teal to orange, while dragging outward shrinks it to a dash — magnitude grows rapidly as r decreases but direction always stays toward the origin

interactions.label: Arrow view
interactions.teaches: Separating magnitude from direction: in direction-only view all arrows are equal-length, revealing the pure attractive radial pattern, while the scaled view adds the inverse-square strength coloring

demo_steps.title: Strong near the source
demo_steps.narration: The sample point sits close to the origin (r ≈ 0.4). Its vector is long and orange — in the scaled view, arrows near the sphere are by far the longest, showing |g| ∝ 1/r².

demo_steps.title: Weak far away
demo_steps.narration: Drag the sample point out to r ≈ 2.5. Its arrow shrinks to a small teal dash, mirroring how arrows near the cube corners are barely visible.

demo_steps.title: Direction alone
demo_steps.narration: Switching to direction-only makes every arrow the same length. The pattern that remains is purely radial attraction — all arrows point at the central mass — with magnitude removed.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cube is 4×4×4 world units, centered at the origin, edges spanning ±2. Axes extend to ±3 with arrowheads; +Z screen-up, +Y screen-right, +X screen-lower-left (standard right-handed math orientation as in the source). Origin sphere: radius 0.15, gradient-shaded blue (#4d7fc4 to #9fc0e8), label '0' offset ~0.25 units below-right. Field arrows sampled on a grid at coordinate values ±0.7, ±1.4, ±2.0 in each axis (6³ = 216 candidate points), skipping positions with |r| < 0.45 so arrows don't overlap the sphere. Each arrow at position p points along −p/|p| (toward origin). Magnitude model: g ∝ 1/r² with normalized length L = clamp(k/r²) where k ≈ 0.35, capped at 0.9 world units and floored at 0.04 so far arrows become tiny dashes exactly as in the source. Color ramp by length/radius: r < 0.9 → orange #e05a19; 0.9 ≤ r < 1.6 → teal #1b93a1; r ≥ 1.6 → dark desaturated teal #12646d. Sample point: a larger marker (~0.09 radius) on the +Y axis, moved by the slider; its dedicated arrow is drawn thicker with a bigger head, cap ~1.8 units, with an on-canvas readout 'r = …, |g| ∝ 1/r² = …'. Cube edge color light blue #8fc2d9; axes black #111111; axis labels italic bold.
interactionPlan.notes: Render arrows as a shaft (cylinder or Line2) plus cone head, oriented so the head points at the origin. Use the same geometry for both views: direction-only merely normalizes all lengths to a fixed ~0.15 units and drops the color ramp to a single teal, so the toggle is a length/color recompute, not a rebuild. The sample arrow and its r / |g| readout must recompute reactively on every slider change. Clamp the sample's minimum r so its scaled arrow does not clip into the origin sphere.

Reduce the visual footprint of the added sample marker/readout so it doesn't distract from the source's pure field depiction
